preceding_source_definitions.348_6.3.1: The natural group homomorphism ch:I(A)=1+completed A^+→completed A_Q^+ is determined on the universal weight-one element by ch(1+X)=exp(X)-1.
preceding_source_definitions.348_eta: eta(sum_(r>=1)a_r t^r)=sum_(r>=1)((-1)^(r-1)/(r-1)!) a_r t^r; t records homogeneous degree.
preceding_source_definitions.348_6.3.2: ch(phi)=eta(Log phi). Log(phi) and eta(Log phi) both have constant0.
preceding_source_definitions.345_unit_and_rank: Ch(A)=K×I(A), with additive zero(0,1), multiplicative unit(1,1), augmentation/rank pi(a,phi)=a, ideal inclusion i(phi)=(0,phi), and scalar inclusion j(a)=(a,1).
preceding_source_definitions.345_multiplication: (a,phi)(b,psi)=(ab,phi^b psi^a(phi*psi)). In particular i(phi)i(psi)=i(phi*psi), while(1,phi)(1,psi)=(1,phi psi(phi*psi)).
preceding_source_definitions.349_6.3.3: The extended character is ch(a,phi)=a+eta(Log phi). Thus ch(i(phi))=eta(Log phi), whereas ch(1,phi)=1+eta(Log phi).
preceding_source_definitions.349_6.5.1: For n>=1 the degree-n subgroup is the image u↦(0,1+u), with u in product_(r>=n)A^r. The phi/psi of6.5(i),(ii) are in this rank-zero ideal.

three_constants.printed: 1+c_p Z_p+...=(1+c_m X_m+...)(1+c_n Y_n+...), with the final diplomatic tail printed as two dots.
three_constants.corrected: c_p Z_p+...=(c_m X_m+...)(c_n Y_n+...), c_r=(-1)^(r-1)/(r-1)!; only the three1+ prefixes are removed by this decision.
three_constants.map: Apply the same ring homomorphism ch to i(phi)i(psi)=i(phi*psi). Every resulting series has scalar/constant0; this directly gives the corrected equality.
three_constants.unit_comparison: Applying ch to the rank-one pairs instead would give(1+ch(phi))(1+ch(psi))=1+ch(phi)+ch(psi)+ch(phi*psi), using their exact product(1,phi psi(phi*psi)). Hence the three printed prefixes cannot be justified by changing the rank convention alone.
three_constants.counterexample: K=Z,A=Z[X,Y],wtX=wtY=1,m=n=1,phi=1+X,psi=1+Y. Formula6.1.1 gives phi*psi=(1+X+Y)/((1+X)(1+Y))=1-XY+terms of degree>=3. The printed left side has degree-one coefficient0, while its right side has X+Y. Under [X]:Q[[X,Y]]→Q these coefficients are0 and1.
three_constants.leading_coefficient: The corrected identity gives p=m+n and c_(m+n) Z_(m+n)=c_m c_n X_mY_n, hence Z_(m+n)=-(m+n-1)!/((m-1)!(n-1)!) X_mY_n, exactly6.5.3. Torsion-free universal coefficients embed into their rational extension; equality then descends and specializes by the independent-coefficient evaluation map.

rational_modulus.printed: ch(phi) congruent ch(1+a_n) mod completed A^(>=n+1).
rational_modulus.scalar_extension: iota_r:A^r→A^r tensor_ZQ sends a↦a tensor1; its product over r>=n+1 maps the integral degree tail into the rational degree tail.
rational_modulus.filtration_map: Log(phi)-Log(1+a_n) has no homogeneous components through n. Applying eta preserves each degree and multiplies it by c_r in Q, so its image lies in product_(r>=n+1)(A^r tensor_ZQ).
rational_modulus.counterexample: K=Z,A=Z[Y],wtY=3,n=1,phi=1+Y,a1=0. The degree-three component is eta(Y)=Y/2. The coordinate projection coefficient_Y sends the image of the integral completion to Z, but sends this difference to1/2. Thus the printed integral modulus fails, while the corrected rational degree>=2 modulus holds.
rational_modulus.scope: Only the opening modulus gains Q; all degree bounds and the printed character map remain unchanged.

disposition: Diplomatic retains both source readings. Current makes the exact three constant removals and one rational-target restoration; no new statement or hypothesis is introduced.
